cancer_indication: Hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative (HR+/HER2–) metastatic breast cancer in combination with endocrine therapy after prior aromatase inhibitor failure.
moa: Everolimus is an oral inhibitor of the mTOR kinase that allosterically inhibits the mTORC1 complex. It binds FKBP12 to form a drug–protein complex that docks on mTORC1 and prevents mTOR activation, reducing phosphorylation of S6K1 and 4E-BP1 and suppressing protein synthesis and cell-cycle progression. In HR+ breast cancer, PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling is frequently hyperactivated as an adaptive escape from hormone dependence; inhibiting mTORC1 can interrupt this survival pathway and restore sensitivity to endocrine therapy. In ER+ models, everolimus treatment reduced ER mRNA/protein and transcriptional activity, supporting synergy with endocrine therapy.

HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.description: Core growth and survival signaling cascade linking PI3K and AKT to mTOR, regulating proliferation, metabolism, and survival.
HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.interpretation: Frequently dysregulated in breast cancer (e.g., via PIK3CA mutation or PTEN loss) and implicated in proliferation and endocrine therapy resistance.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Baseline hyperactive PI3K–AKT–mTOR suggests growth dependence on mTORC1 outputs; mTORC1 inhibition is more likely to suppress proliferation in HR+ settings (often with endocrine partner).:contentReference[oaicite:3]{index=3}
NCT00863655; PMID:22149876; DrugBank:DB01590; ChEMBL:CHEMBL1908360
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: “Up” may reflect strong upstream RTK/AKT signaling poised for feedback rebound; PI3K/AKT reactivation can maintain survival despite mTORC1 blockade (classic rapalog escape).:contentReference[oaicite:4]{index=4}:contentReference[oaicite:5]{index=5}
PMID:25537515 (MYC escape context); DrugBank:DB01590

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Low pathway score yet residual mTORC1-addiction can still exist (e.g., translational control) and respond; uncommon because most responders show pathway engagement.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: If PI3K–AKT–mTOR is not a driver, mTORC1 inhibition is less impactful and other oncogenic programs dominate.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Everolimus suppresses mTORC1 downstream signaling → reduced proliferation/translation programs (on-target pharmacodynamics).:contentReference[oaicite:6]{index=6}
DrugBank:DB01590; PMID:22149876
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Even with apparent pathway downshift, tumors can persist via bypass (MYC programs, autophagic survival, or alternate RTK routes), producing clinical resistance despite target inhibition.:contentReference[oaicite:7]{index=7}:contentReference[oaicite:8]{index=8}

Sensitive: Mechanistically unlikely: Post-treatment ‘Up’ usually represents compensatory feedback rather than effective killing; sensitivity despite upshift would typically require strong combination suppression elsewhere (rare).:contentReference[oaicite:9]{index=9}
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: mTORC1 inhibition relieves S6K–IRS1 feedback → AKT/RTK rebound and PI3K pathway reactivation, driving escape/resistance.:contentReference[oaicite:10]{index=10}:contentReference[oaicite:11]{index=11}
DrugBank:DB01590

HALLMARK_MTORC1_SIGNALING.description: mTORC1 downstream output program controlling cap-dependent translation, ribosomal biogenesis, and growth-related protein synthesis (e.g., via S6K and 4E-BP1).
HALLMARK_MTORC1_SIGNALING.interpretation: Represents the translational and proliferative output of mTORC1 activity that supports breast tumor growth and cell-cycle progression.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: High mTORC1 output indicates target engagement/addiction; rapalog inhibition is more likely to yield antiproliferative benefit.:contentReference[oaicite:12]{index=12}
PMID:22149876; NCT00863655; DrugBank:DB01590
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate (common limitation): mTORC1 ‘Up’ can coexist with incomplete 4EBP1 control and/or rapid bypass activation (AKT/MYC/autophagy), limiting depth/duration of response.:contentReference[oaicite:13]{index=13}

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Low signature but residual mTORC1 dependency can remain at protein/translation level; uncommon.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: If baseline mTORC1 is not active, an mTORC1 inhibitor has less leverage on growth.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Direct on-target suppression of mTORC1 signaling is the intended therapeutic mechanism.:contentReference[oaicite:14]{index=14}
DrugBank:DB01590; PMID:22149876
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Target is inhibited but tumor survives using escape programs (MYC-driven proliferation, autophagy-mediated stress tolerance, upstream RTK/AKT rebound).:contentReference[oaicite:15]{index=15}:contentReference[oaicite:16]{index=16}

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible (direct effect): Everolimus inhibits mTORC1; a true sustained ‘Up’ would imply no effective drug exposure or assay artifact.
DrugBank:DB01590
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate (if observed): Apparent ‘Up’ indicates lack of target inhibition (PK/PD failure) → resistance by definition.
DrugBank:DB01590

WP_ESTROGEN_SIGNALING.description: Estrogen receptor (ER) signaling program driving estrogen-responsive transcription and ER-dependent proliferation in hormone receptor-positive breast cancer.
WP_ESTROGEN_SIGNALING.interpretation: A central dependency in HR+ breast cancer and a key axis of endocrine response/resistance with documented cross-talk to PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate (HR+ context): Active ER signaling provides endocrine synergy; everolimus + endocrine therapy can restore/augment hormone sensitivity after AI failure.:contentReference[oaicite:17]{index=17}:contentReference[oaicite:18]{index=18}
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: If ER activity is driven by strong ligand-independent programs and co-drivers (RTKs/MYC), mTORC1 blockade may not fully suppress ER output → reduced benefit.
PMID:27421652 :contentReference[oaicite:19]{index=19}

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: ER-low tumors are not the classic everolimus + endocrine population; sensitivity here would typically depend on non-ER mTOR addiction (less common).
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate (HR+ regimen logic): Absence/downregulation of ER signaling undermines endocrine synergy and is associated with poor benefit in endocrine-augmentation use-cases.:contentReference[oaicite:20]{index=20}

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Everolimus can reduce ER expression/activity (mTOR-dependent translation/chaperoning), supporting endocrine re-sensitization in ER+ disease.:contentReference[oaicite:21]{index=21} :contentReference[oaicite:22]{index=22}
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: If ER pathway becomes suppressed due to phenotypic switch/ER loss, the endocrine partner loses efficacy and the combo strategy fails (clinical resistance scenario).:contentReference[oaicite:23]{index=23}

Sensitive: Mechanistically unlikely: Everolimus does not directly activate ER signaling; sensitivity with ER ‘Up’ would more likely reflect endocrine partner effects rather than everolimus.
Resistance: Mechanistically plausible: Compensatory ER transcriptional rebound can sustain growth despite mTORC1 inhibition, particularly if upstream cues remain strong.

HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS.description: E2F-regulated transcriptional program supporting DNA replication and cell-cycle progression (G1/S and S-phase gene expression).
HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS.interpretation: Reflects proliferative cell-cycle activity in breast tumors and is modulated downstream of growth and translation control pathways.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: High E2F/proliferation implies reliance on biosynthetic/cell-cycle programs supported by mTORC1; inhibition often yields G1 arrest and reduced proliferation.:contentReference[oaicite:24]{index=24}
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: If E2F is driven by RB1 loss/uncoupled cell-cycle control, mTORC1 inhibition may not enforce durable arrest → reduced sensitivity.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Low proliferation tumors can still respond if survival depends on mTORC1 translation outputs rather than cell-cycle speed.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Cytostatic benefit is limited when baseline proliferation is already low; pathway not a dependency.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Everolimus suppresses cell-cycle drivers (including E2F target programs) consistent with antiproliferative on-target effects.:contentReference[oaicite:25]{index=25}
DrugBank:DB01590
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: E2F reduction can be cytostatic without tumor clearance; survival escape (autophagy/MYC/AKT rebound) still yields resistance.:contentReference[oaicite:26]{index=26}

Sensitive: Mechanistically unlikely: Persistent/high E2F after mTORC1 inhibition usually indicates failure to arrest, not sensitivity.
DrugBank:DB01590
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Lack of E2F suppression reflects ineffective cell-cycle control under therapy → resistance.
DrugBank:DB01590

GOBP_PROCESS_UTILIZING_AUTOPHAGIC_MECHAN.description: Autophagy-related cellular process enabling degradation and recycling of cellular components under stress conditions.
GOBP_PROCESS_UTILIZING_AUTOPHAGIC_MECHAN.interpretation: Acts as an adaptive stress-response program in breast cancer cells under therapeutic pressure and can support survival under mTORC1 inhibition.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: In select contexts, very high autophagy can become cytotoxic (‘autophagic cell death’) when further induced; uncommon in breast cancer under rapalogs.
PMID:27421652 :contentReference[oaicite:27]{index=27}
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Baseline high autophagy provides stress tolerance and can blunt mTORC1-inhibitor efficacy (survival adaptation).:contentReference[oaicite:28]{index=28}
PMID:27421652 :contentReference[oaicite:29]{index=29}

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low autophagy capacity reduces ability to buffer metabolic stress from mTORC1 inhibition → higher likelihood of response.
PMID:27421652 :contentReference[oaicite:30]{index=30}
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Tumor may rely on alternate stress programs (MYC/AKT) independent of autophagy; autophagy-low yet resistant is possible but not the classic pattern.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: If autophagy induction is excessive and pushes cells beyond tolerance, it can contribute to cell death; not the dominant breast-cancer phenotype under everolimus.:contentReference[oaicite:31]{index=31}
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Everolimus induces autophagy by relieving mTORC1 repression; in breast cancer this often functions as a survival mechanism promoting resistance.:contentReference[oaicite:32]{index=32} :contentReference[oaicite:33]{index=33}

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Autophagy down after everolimus would usually require co-therapy (autophagy inhibitors), which can enhance sensitivity (combination-dependent).
Resistance: Mechanistically plausible: Even if autophagy is suppressed, resistance can persist via MYC/AKT-driven escape programs.

HALLMARK_MYC_TARGETS_V1.description: MYC-driven transcriptional program regulating metabolism, biosynthesis, and proliferation-associated gene expression.
HALLMARK_MYC_TARGETS_V1.interpretation: MYC pathway activity is implicated in sustaining growth programs that can bypass growth-inhibitory signaling constraints in breast cancer models under targeted therapy.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: High MYC tumors are usually aggressive and may show transient cytostasis from mTORC1 inhibition, but durable sensitivity is uncommon if MYC remains dominant.
PMID:25537515 :contentReference[oaicite:34]{index=34}
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: High MYC activity (or MYC amplification/signature) is a validated escape/bypass program associated with everolimus resistance in ER+ models.:contentReference[oaicite:35]{index=35} :contentReference[oaicite:36]{index=36}

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low MYC reduces bypass capacity; tumors may be more reliant on mTORC1-controlled growth programs and respond better.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: MYC-low yet resistant can occur if other bypass pathways dominate (RTK/AKT feedback, etc.).

Sensitive: Mechanistically unlikely: Therapy-induced MYC upshift typically marks adaptation/escape rather than sensitivity.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Everolimus pressure can select/induce MYC program activation (epigenetic BRD4→MYC) sustaining proliferation despite mTORC1 blockade.:contentReference[oaicite:37]{index=37} :contentReference[oaicite:38]{index=38}

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare (combination-dependent): If MYC is suppressed (e.g., via BET/BRD4 targeting), tumors can be resensitized to everolimus.
PMID:25537515 :contentReference[oaicite:39]{index=39}
Resistance: Mechanistically plausible: Even with MYC controlled, resistance can arise from PI3K/AKT rebound or immune-evasion/autophagy programs.
PMID:27421652; DrugBank:DB01590

KEGG_MEDICUS_REFERENCE_IGF_IGF1R_PI3K_SI.description: Growth-factor signaling from IGF ligands through IGF1R to PI3K/AKT pathway activation.
KEGG_MEDICUS_REFERENCE_IGF_IGF1R_PI3K_SI.interpretation: A growth-factor input into PI3K/AKT signaling that can be engaged as a compensatory route when downstream mTORC1 signaling is inhibited.

Sensitive: Mechanistically plausible: Upstream IGF/IGF1R signaling feeds PI3K; if tumor remains mTORC1-dependent downstream, everolimus may still suppress growth (often partial).
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: High IGF1R/RTK activity predisposes to feedback-driven AKT hyperactivation on rapalog therapy, a known resistance route.:contentReference[oaicite:40]{index=40}:contentReference[oaicite:41]{index=41}
DrugBank:DB01590

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low IGF1R drive reduces likelihood of strong AKT rebound; mTORC1 inhibition is more likely to translate into growth suppression.
Resistance: Mechanistically plausible: Resistance can still occur via MYC or autophagy even without IGF1R dependence.

Sensitive: Mechanistically plausible (context-dependent): If upstream IGF signaling is not induced (or is co-inhibited), AKT rebound is blunted and response improves.
DrugBank:DB01590
Resistance: Mechanistically plausible: Even with IGF axis low, tumors can escape via HER-family signaling or MYC/autophagy programs.

Sensitive: Mechanistically unlikely: IGF1R/PI3K upregulation after therapy usually represents compensatory escape rather than sensitivity.
DrugBank:DB01590
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Everolimus relieves feedback inhibition on insulin/IGF and HER receptors, increasing AKT phosphorylation and driving resistance.:contentReference[oaicite:42]{index=42}
DrugBank:DB01590

HALLMARK_ANGIOGENESIS.description: Angiogenesis program involving hypoxia-driven and VEGF-associated pathways that support neovascularization and tumor perfusion.
HALLMARK_ANGIOGENESIS.interpretation: Tumor vascularization supports nutrient delivery and growth, and angiogenic signaling can influence tumor progression across breast cancer contexts.

Sensitive: Mechanistically plausible: Highly angiogenic tumors may be more impacted by mTOR–HIF–VEGF suppression, reducing vascular support and growth (supporting sensitivity).
PMID:36745547 :contentReference[oaicite:43]{index=43}
Resistance: Mechanistically plausible: Angiogenesis can be driven by non-mTOR programs (e.g., alternate pro-angiogenic cytokines), so baseline ‘Up’ does not guarantee everolimus benefit.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Low angiogenesis is not a specific sensitizer; sensitivity would come from direct tumor-cell mTOR addiction rather than vascular effects.
Resistance: Mechanistically plausible: If angiogenesis is already low, vascular suppression adds little; resistance depends on other drivers.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Everolimus can downregulate HIF-1α/VEGF signaling, decreasing microvessel support as part of antitumor effect.:contentReference[oaicite:44]{index=44} :contentReference[oaicite:45]{index=45}
Resistance: Mechanistically plausible: Despite reduced angiogenesis signature, tumors may survive via metabolic adaptation/autophagy or alternative angiogenic routes.

Sensitive: Mechanistically unlikely: Post-treatment angiogenesis upshift usually indicates failure of vascular suppression and predicts poor response.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Reactivation/compensation of angiogenic programs undermines growth suppression and supports resistance.:contentReference[oaicite:46]{index=46}

KEGG_MEDICUS_REFERENCE_PDL_PD1_SHP_PI3K_.description: Immune checkpoint signaling centered on the PD-1/PD-L1 axis associated with suppression of anti-tumor immune activity.
KEGG_MEDICUS_REFERENCE_PDL_PD1_SHP_PI3K_.interpretation: Immune evasion through checkpoint signaling is relevant to tumor microenvironment control in breast cancer, particularly in immune-infiltrated contexts.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Baseline checkpoint activation does not sensitize to everolimus; any apparent sensitivity would be indirect (e.g., vascular/PI3K effects) rather than immune-checkpoint biology.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: An immune-evasive (PD-1/PD-L1-high) microenvironment plus everolimus immunosuppressive effects can blunt anti-tumor immunity, aligning with resistance risk.:contentReference[oaicite:47]{index=47}
PMID:37257766 :contentReference[oaicite:48]{index=48}

Sensitive: Mechanistically plausible: Lower baseline checkpoint signaling implies less immune evasion; everolimus’ immune suppression is less likely to be the dominant limiting factor (context-dependent).
Resistance: Mechanistically plausible: Even PD-L1-low tumors can be resistant through tumor-intrinsic MYC/autophagy/AKT escape mechanisms.

Sensitive: Mechanistically plausible (combination-dependent): If PD-1/PD-L1 signaling is functionally neutralized (e.g., with anti–PD-1), sensitivity can improve in preclinical TNBC contexts.
PMID:37257766 :contentReference[oaicite:49]{index=49}
Resistance: Mechanistically plausible: Checkpoint pathway may be ‘down’ yet tumor still escapes via intrinsic resistance (MYC/AKT/autophagy).

Sensitive: Mechanistically unlikely: Everolimus-associated PD-L1 upregulation generally marks immune escape unless countered by checkpoint blockade.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Everolimus can increase PD-L1 and reduce CD8+ infiltration (preclinical TNBC), creating an immune-evasive state associated with resistance unless PD-1 blockade is added.:contentReference[oaicite:50]{index=50} :contentReference[oaicite:51]{index=51}

sensitivity_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: PI3K pathway alterations (including PIK3CA mutation) are described as hyperactivating PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling in breast cancer, a context in which tumors can be more dependent on the pathway targeted downstream by mTORC1 inhibition.

Retention of ER signaling/ER expression in HR+ disease is described as part of the endocrine-responsive context in which everolimus is used to overcome endocrine resistance when combined with endocrine therapy.

sensitivity_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: PTEN loss is described as a frequent event (notably in TNBC) that leads to unchecked AKT/mTOR pathway activation and was cited as a feature of tumors most likely to benefit in the everolimus + carboplatin TNBC trial context.

resistance_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: Acquired everolimus resistance in ER+ breast cancer models is described as being driven by upregulation of c-MYC and enrichment of MYC target signatures; MYC knockdown resensitized resistant cells.
Upregulation of IGF1R and related upstream signaling is described as contributing to compensatory AKT rephosphorylation after mTORC1 inhibition, supporting resistance.
EGFR is listed among receptor tyrosine kinases that can be upregulated as part of compensatory signaling leading to AKT/parallel pathway activation and resistance.
HER2 signaling is described as a potential upstream driver whose compensatory activity can contribute to PI3K/AKT reactivation and reduced response to everolimus in certain contexts.
Increased HER3–PI3K signaling is described as correlating with everolimus non-response in HER2+ tumors, consistent with RTK/AKT upregulation as a resistance driver.
Anti-apoptotic proteins such as BCL-2 are described as being overexpressed in some everolimus-resistant cells, supporting survival under therapeutic stress.
Survivin (BIRC5) is described as upregulated in everolimus-resistant breast cancer cells and contributing to resistance by helping cells avoid death.

resistance_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: Downregulation or loss of ER signaling in formerly ER+ disease is described as conferring resistance to everolimus plus endocrine therapy because the combination relies on concurrent hormone blockade to be effective in ER+ cancer.

Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HR+/HER2– (Luminal A/B) Subtype: Postmenopausal women with HR+ HER2– advanced breast cancer that progressed on nonsteroidal AIs benefited from everolimus + exemestane, as shown in the BOLERO-2 trial; everolimus is integrated into guidelines for endocrine-resistant HR+ disease.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HER2-Positive Subtype: Everolimus has been studied in combination with anti-HER2 therapy in resistant cases; BOLERO-3 showed a modest but significant PFS improvement and exploratory analyses suggested benefit concentrated in HR-negative/HER2+ tumors.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.Triple-Negative (TNBC) Subtype: Everolimus is not an established treatment in TNBC outside clinical trials; a randomized phase II study of everolimus + carboplatin vs carboplatin reported improved PFS and noted tumors most likely to benefit were those with mTOR pathway activation (e.g., PTEN loss).
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.BRCA-mutated/HRD Subtype: There is no dedicated trial of everolimus in BRCA-mutant patients and no specific evidence that BRCA/HRD status predicts better or worse response; the text emphasizes PI3K pathway status as more relevant than HRD itself.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.Basal-like vs. Luminal vs. HER2-enriched: Basal-like overlaps with TNBC (with PTEN loss in subsets); HER2-enriched overlaps with HER2+/HR– where a signal of benefit was observed; luminal A/B overlaps with HR+ where everolimus has the most established role.
